title: Bounded injective model of module derived Hom and its upper support bound
statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative ring. Write $Q$ for localization of integer-indexed cochain complexes of $A$-modules into $D(A)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let $I$ be a complex of injective $A$-modules [def-sp-injective-resolutions], and let $a\leq b$ be integers with $I^q=0$ outside $[a,b]$. For every complex $M$, there is a canonical isomorphism in $D(A)$
$$\theta_M:R\operatorname{Hom}_A(QM,QI)\xrightarrow{\sim}Q\operatorname{Hom}_A^\bullet(M,I),$$
where derived internal Hom [def-pur-derived-internal-hom] is taken on the one-object site with coefficient ring $A$ and only the identity covering [def-pc-ring-hom-extension-shared-definitions], and total Hom is $A$-module-valued [def-sc-module-total-hom-complex]. For every chain map $f:M'\to M$, the comparisons satisfy
$$Q(f^*)\circ\theta_M=\theta_{M'}\circ R\operatorname{Hom}_A(Qf,QI).$$
If, in addition, $M^p=0$ for $p<n$ for an integer $n$, then $\operatorname{Hom}_A^r(M,I)=0$ and $H^rR\operatorname{Hom}_A(QM,QI)=0$ for every $r>b-n$. No finiteness or Noetherian hypothesis is assumed.

proof.text: On the one-object site there is just one value and no nontrivial restriction or sheaf condition. Thus a module sheaf is an $A$-module, sheaf Hom is $A$-linear Hom, and products are products of modules. The formula for the sheaf Hom complex therefore becomes exactly $\operatorname{Hom}_A^r(M,I)=\prod_p\operatorname{Hom}_A(M^p,I^{p+r})$ with differential $d_Iz-(-1)^rzd_M$, including its $A$-action. The identity on every component identifies these complexes and their pre- and postcomposition maps.

source.place: Tags 0A8X (section-hom-complexes), 08J7 (section-internal-hom); evaluation on the one-object identity-covering site.

proof.text: Since $I^q=0$ for $q<a$ and every $I^q$ is injective, the bounded-below-injectives lemma makes $I$ K-injective. Let $\eta:I\to J(I)$ be the fixed K-injective resolution used in the definition of derived internal Hom. For each $M$, that definition supplies the localization comparison $c_M:R\operatorname{Hom}_A(QM,QI)\xrightarrow{\sim}Q\operatorname{Hom}_A^\bullet(M,J(I))$. Apply Hom-complex invariance with $s=\eta$ and $t=1_M$: both targets are K-injective, and both maps are quasi-isomorphisms. Hence $u_M=Q\operatorname{Hom}_A^\bullet(M,\eta)$ is invertible. Define $\theta_M=u_M^{-1}c_M$. This uses the fixed resolution unit, so gives the canonical comparison, without choosing a new resolution or an arbitrary isomorphism.

For $f:M'\to M$, write $v=Q\operatorname{Hom}_A^\bullet(f,I)$ and $w=Q\operatorname{Hom}_A^\bullet(f,J(I))$. Componentwise, $\eta(zf)=(\eta z)f$, giving $u_{M'}v=wu_M$. The definition by localization gives $wc_M=c_{M'}R\operatorname{Hom}_A(Qf,QI)$, since the first-variable action is precomposition before localization. Multiplying these equalities by the inverses of $u_M$ and $u_{M'}$ gives $v\theta_M=\theta_{M'}R\operatorname{Hom}_A(Qf,QI)$, the required naturality identity.

source.place: Tags 0A8X (section-hom-complexes), 08J7 (section-internal-hom): functor on the product localization.

proof.text: Assume $M^p=0$ for $p<n$ and fix $r>b-n$. In the product formula, for $p<n$ the source of the factor $\operatorname{Hom}_A(M^p,I^{p+r})$ is zero; for $p\geq n$ one has $p+r>b$, so its target is zero. Every factor is therefore the zero module, and their product is the zero module (its only family is the zero family). Thus $\operatorname{Hom}_A^r(M,I)=0$. Its $r$-th cohomology is then zero by the kernel/image formula, and the cohomology functor applied to $\theta_M$ identifies this with $H^rR\operatorname{Hom}_A(QM,QI)$.
